A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

11-cRBA is a specific and potent inactivator for the isomerohydrlase activity, and that the isomerohydrase is a membrane protein with an estimated molecular weight of approximately 40-45 kDa, based on the labeling pattern of crude membranes.
the RPE isomerohydralase is a 11-cis-specific enzyme that is distinct from LRAT and is not a retinyl ester synthase.
the RPE isomerohydrlase activity is a protein that can be specifically labeled by 11-cRBA and that this protein may be an essential component of the isomerization reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
11-cRBA inactivation of RPE isomerohydrlase activity is a specific and sensitive assay for the identification of this enzyme.
11-cRBA is a useful tool in studying the isomerohydralse activity and the mechanism of the isomerization reaction.
the isomerohydrlase activity, which is critical for rhodopsin synthesis, is not an inherent property of all-trans-retinal, but rather an activity mediated by a specific enzyme.
